question: In the INREV Due Diligence Questionnaire 2022 for Funds of Funds and Multi Manager, when was the FoF / MM questionnaire originally launched, what two additions appear at the front of the DDQ, and how long may the manager's statement be?
gold_answer: The INREV FoF / MM DDQ was originally launched in 2014 as a variation of the INREV DDQ for Non-Listed Real Estate Investment Vehicles (most recently updated in 2018). The two additions at the front are (i) a Vehicle Fact Sheet, a snapshot of basic high-level vehicle information, and (ii) a Funds of Funds / Multi Manager Statement, where the manager showcases its platform and expertise. The statement should be short, no more than one page.
gold_passage: Originally launched in 2014, INREV FoF / MM is a variation of the INREV Due Diligence Questionnaire for Non-Listed Real Estate Investment Vehicles (INREV DDQ) most recently updated in 2018. | (i) a Vehicle Fact Sheet - providing a snapshot of the basic high-level vehicle information; and | (ii) a Funds of Funds / Multi Manager Statement - giving the manager the opportunity to showcase its platform and expertise. | This statement should be short, no more than one page,
notes: Introduction and statement page of the 2022 docx. Distractor: the 2018 non-listed INREV DDQ has an 'Investment Manager Statement' in place of the FoF / MM Statement, with the same one-page limit, and was launched in April 2007 (already asked in DDQ-05). The protocol as a whole dates from April 2007; 2014 is the launch of the FoF / MM variation.

question: A 2021 covering note describes an update to a responsible-investment due diligence questionnaire for private equity limited partners. When was the first version of that questionnaire launched, who adopted it, when was the working group for the update set up, and over how long had LPs and GPs been giving comments?
gold_answer: The PRI Limited Partners Private Equity Responsible Investment DDQ was first launched in 2015 and adopted by ILPA as part of the broader ILPA DDQ. The PRI set up a working group of PRI signatories in early 2021. LPs and GPs had given comments, written and verbal, over the past four months. The updated ESG DDQ is Section 19 of the ILPA DDQ.
gold_passage: The first version of the PRI Limited Partners Private Equity Responsible Investment Due Diligence Questionnaire (DDQ) was launched in 2015 and adopted by ILPA as part of the broader ILPA DDQ. | In early 2021, the PRI established a working group comprised of PRI signatories | Over the past four months, both the LPs and GPs involved have provided significant amounts of comments, both written and verbally.
notes: The document is not named in the question. 'launched in 2015' occurs only in the PRI file (grep -il over all 81 files). 'four months' also matches SFERS, but in an unrelated context. Distractor: ILPA DDQ v1.2 says v1.1 (Sept 2016) was revised to reflect 'PRI's new LP Responsible Investment DDQ'.

question: How many organisations are listed as working group participants in the appendix of the PRI covering note on the 2021 update of its private equity responsible investment DDQ, and who represented CalPERS and CalSTRS?
gold_answer: 31 organisations are listed. CalPERS (California Public Employees' Retirement System) was represented by James Andrus, and CalSTRS (California State Teachers' Retirement System) by Nicholas Abel.
gold_passage: see the full list of working group participants in the appendix | California Public Employees’ Retirement System (CalPERS) – James Andrus | California State Teachers' Retirement System (CalSTRS) – Nicholas Abel
notes: Counted 31 bullets in the APPENDIX (grep -c on the bullet character = 31), from AlpInvest Partners to Universities Superannuation Scheme (USS). Four organisations list two people (Ardian, EQT, HKMA, TPG & Y Analytics), so the number of people is higher than 31. The file uses a curly apostrophe for CalPERS and a straight one for CalSTRS.

question: Which due diligence questionnaire in the corpus asks the manager whether it requires its underlying investments to submit data to sustainability performance evaluation organisations, and which organisation does it give as an example?
gold_answer: The INREV DDQ 2022 for Funds of Funds and Multi Manager, question 3.8.1 (Supplementary Stage, section 3.8 Environmental, Social and Governance). The example given is the Global Real Estate Sustainability Benchmark (GRESB), and the manager is asked for its scores/results if it does require this.
gold_passage: 3.8.1Do you require your underlying investments to submit data to sustainability performance evaluation organisations (e.g. Global Real Estate Sustainability Benchmark)? If so, what are your scores/results?
notes: The document is not named in the question. 'sustainability performance evaluation' appears only in the 2022 docx (grep -il over all 81 files). Near-duplicate distractor: the INREV 2018 non-listed DDQ 3.8.1 asks whether the vehicle itself submits data to GRESB and what its score is. The older INREV FoF .doc has no GRESB or 'sustainab' text, checked after decoding its garbled UTF-16.

question: According to the ILPA Due Diligence Questionnaire v1.2, when was version 1.1 released and what changes did it introduce?
gold_answer: Version 1.1 was released in September 2016. It (1) added new questions on compliance with the ILPA Reporting Template (released January 2016) to the Accounting / Valuation / Reporting sections; (2) revised the original Governance and Risk / Compliance / ESG sections to reflect PRI's new LP Responsible Investment DDQ, and re-ordered, merged and edited existing questions in those sections; and (3) refreshed existing web links, font and formatting as needed.
gold_passage: New in Version 1.1 (released in September 2016) | Added new questions regarding compliance with the ILPA Reporting Template (released in Jan. 2016) to the “Accounting / Valuation / Reporting” sections | Revised the original “Governance” and “Risk / Compliance / ESG” sections to reflect PRI’s new LP Responsible Investment DDQ, and to re-order/merge/edit existing questions from these sections | Refreshed existing web links, font, and formatting, as needed
notes: From the change log on the first page of v1.2. 'Version 1.1' appears only in this file. Do not mix it up with the v1.2 changes (Section 14 Diversity and Inclusion, six new Appendix A documents, clarified Q4.4), which DDQ-06 already covers.

question: One private equity due diligence questionnaire asks whether the fund gives limited partners more than a certain number of business days' notice for capital calls. What is the threshold, and in which section of the questionnaire is this question?
gold_answer: The threshold is more than 10 business days' notice for capital calls, either generally or in specific circumstances (e.g. when a single capital call is above an agreed and stated percentage of total unfunded commitment). It is question 7.14 in Section 7.0 Credit Facilities of the ILPA Due Diligence Questionnaire 2.0.
gold_passage: 7.0 Credit Facilities | 7.14 Does the Fund provide Limited Partners with greater than 10 business days notice for capital calls, either generally or in specific circumstances (such as in cases where a single capital call is above an agreed and stated percentage
notes: The document is not named in the question. '10 business days' appears only in ILPA 2.0 (grep -il over all 81 files). Other files that mention capital calls do not set a notice threshold, e.g. INREV 2022 2.4.9.1 asks only 'How much notification is provided'. ILPA v1.2 has no credit facility section (grep 'credit facilit' = 0).

question: In the INREV Due Diligence Questionnaire for Non-Listed Real Estate Investment Vehicles (2018), which expense ratio must the manager provide under Fees and Expenses, and on what bases?
gold_answer: Question 1.6.2 asks for the INREV Total Expense Ratio (TER): a forward-looking estimate (with the calculation method) if the vehicle has not been launched, or the INREV TER if it is an existing vehicle. The TER must be given on both NAV and GAV, with and without performance fees. If INREV TER is not used, a calculation in line with INREV TER (INREV Fee and Expense Metrics) is required.
gold_passage: If the vehicle has not been launched, please provide a forward-looking estimate of INREV Total Expense Ratio (TER), and how you have calculated it. If the vehicle is an existing vehicle, please provide INREV TER. Please provide the TER based on NAV and GAV, with and without performance fees.
notes: Pair partner XD-08 (INREV FoF / MM 2022 uses 'INREV expense ratio (TGER)'). The difference to test is the metric name: TER in 2018 vs TGER in 2022. The old INREV FoF .doc fact sheet also has 'INREV total expense ratio (TER) (actual or forecast)', but that is a different document.

question: In the INREV Due Diligence Questionnaire 2022 for Funds of Funds and Multi Manager, which expense ratio must the manager provide under Fees and Expenses, and on what bases?
gold_answer: Question 1.6.2 asks for the INREV expense ratio (TGER): a forward-looking estimate (with the calculation method) if the vehicle has not been launched, or the historical INREV expense ratio (TGER) if it is an existing vehicle. It must be given on both NAV and GAV, with and without performance fees. If the INREV expense ratio is not used, a calculation in line with the INREV Fee and Expense Metrics module is required.
gold_passage: If the vehicle has not been launched, please provide a forward-looking estimate of the INREV expense ratio (TGER), and how you have calculated it. If the vehicle is an existing vehicle, please provide the historical INREV expense ratio (TGER). | Please provide the expense ratio based on NAV and GAV, with and without performance fees.
notes: Pair partner XD-07 (2018 non-listed DDQ uses INREV Total Expense Ratio, TER). 'TGER' appears only in the 2022 docx (grep -il over all 81 files).

question: How many lettered appendices does the ILPA Due Diligence Questionnaire v1.2 list in its table of contents, and what are they?
gold_answer: Five appendices (A-E): A - Requested Documents; B - Templates: Team Members; C - Templates: References; D - Templates: Fund; E - Templates: Portfolio Investments.
gold_passage: Appendix A - Requested Documents | Appendix B - Templates: Team Members | Appendix C - Templates: References | Appendix D - Templates: Fund | Appendix E - Templates: Portfolio Investments
notes: From the table of contents at the top of the file (lines 7-11). Pair partner XD-10 (ILPA DDQ 2.0 has 8 appendices, A-H).

question: How many lettered appendices does the ILPA Due Diligence Questionnaire 2.0 list in its table of contents, and what are they?
gold_answer: Eight appendices (A-H): A - Requested Documents; B - Templates: Team Members; C - Templates: References; D - Templates: Third-Party(s) and Technology Tool(s); E - Templates: Fund; F - Templates: Portfolio Investments; G - Templates: GP-Led Secondaries / Continuation Funds; H - Templates: Credit Facilities. Compared with v1.2, the new ones are the Third-Party/Technology, GP-Led Secondaries / Continuation Funds and Credit Facilities templates, and the Fund and Portfolio Investments templates move to E and F.
gold_passage: Appendix D - Templates: Third-Party(s) and Technology Tool(s) | Appendix E - Templates: Fund | Appendix F - Templates: Portfolio Investments | Appendix G - Templates: GP-Led Secondaries / Continuation Funds | Appendix H - Templates: Credit Facilities
notes: From the table of contents (lines 9-16). The passage leaves out A-C because they are the same as in v1.2. Pair partner XD-09 (v1.2 has 5 appendices).

question: What questions does the INREV DDQ 2022 for Funds of Funds and Multi Manager ask under section 3.3 'IT, Cyber and Physical Security'?
gold_answer: Fourteen questions (3.3.1-3.3.14): (1) position, responsibilities and members of the IT function, and an overview of outsourced IT and how vendors are monitored; (2) compliance with ISO 27001 or other cyber/information security certifications; (3) whether IT and physical security is a standing board agenda item; (4) a formal, documented Cyber Incident Response Plan; (5) any material cyber/information security incident in the past three years; (6) approved antivirus on all servers, workstations and remote devices; (7) how often staff get IT security training; (8) phishing/social engineering tests on staff; (9) how often full (physical and system) vulnerability assessments are done; (10) how often internal and external penetration tests are done; (11) critical/high-risk findings outstanding for over six months; (12) an external cyber security specialist engaged as first point of contact; (13) how physical access to the server/communication room is controlled; (14) a policy on physical access outside standard office hours, e.g. whether permanent staff are on the premises when third-party suppliers work.
gold_passage: 3.3IT, Cyber and Physical Security | 3.3.1Describe the position, responsibilities, and members of the IT function in the organisation. | 3.3.4Have you developed a formal, documented Cyber Incident Response Plan that describes workflow in the event of a cyber incident? | 3.3.10How frequently are internal and external penetration tests carried out? | 3.3.14Do you have a policy regarding physical access around non-standard office hours?
notes: Docx lines 839-867. Near-duplicate distractor: the INREV 2018 non-listed DDQ section 3.3 has 13 questions. It has no IT-function question, so it starts with ISO 27001, and its last question asks whether permanent staff are always on the premises 'when the cleaners are working'. 'non-standard office hours' appears only in the 2022 docx and 'cleaners' only in the 2018 PDF.

question: What 'Red Flag Questions' does the Calamos/Aksia Private Markets Due Diligence Questionnaire tell investors to ask a manager?
gold_answer: Five red flag questions: (1) Have any senior investment professionals left in the last 5 years? (2) Is there any history of client complaints, regulatory actions or pending litigation against the firm or its principals? (3) What is the current capacity limit, and at what asset level would growth impair the ability to keep deploying the strategy? (4) What might cause the manager to close the fund to new investors? (5) What is the biggest risk to the strategy that 'keeps you up at night'?
gold_passage: Red Flag Questions | Have any senior investment professionals left in the | or pending litigation against your firm or its principals? | What do you believe the current capacity limit is, | What might cause you to close this fund to new investors? | What’s the biggest risk to your strategy that keeps you
notes: The PDF has two columns that are interleaved in the text extraction, so the passage uses short fragments from the right-hand column under 'Red Flag Questions' (lines 84-100). 'Red Flag' appears only in this file.

question: What does the ILPA Due Diligence Questionnaire 2.0 ask about GP-led secondaries and continuation funds in Section 6?
gold_answer: Section 6.0 opens with two Yes/No screening questions. 6.1 asks whether the Firm has done a GP-led secondary in the last five years, and 6.2 asks the same for a continuation fund transaction. Each has four follow-ups: did the LPAC review conflicts in every transaction; was a status quo option available to existing LPs in every transaction; was GP carry rolled over at 100% in every transaction; and were portfolio companies in an IPO or pre-IPO process excluded. Narrative questions 6.3-6.11 then cover: how conflicts of interest are reviewed with the LPAC and LPs (timing, information, Firm benefits not accruing to LPs, transparency on LPAC members or affiliates acting as acquirers); the information given to the LPAC/LPs and its timing; how new fund documents and side letters are structured; the options offered to LPs, including status quo, and differences for new or 'rolling' LPs; the impact on GP economics, alignment of interests and Key Person provisions; the rationale for this route rather than a fund extension or traditional exit; how the bidding universe and valuations are set (secondary managers, third-party advisers, valuation providers); fee structuring (broken deal/termination fees, sharing of transaction costs, management fee, carry); and disclosure of related deals between the GP and acquirers (e.g. stapled transactions or side deals).
gold_passage: 6.0 GP-Led Secondaries / Continuation Funds | 6.1.2 Was there a status quo option available for existing Limited Partners in every transaction? | 6.1.3 Was General Partner carry rolled over at 100% in every transaction? | 6.8 Describe how the Firm develops the rationale for the transactions to take place via a fund restructuring, GP-led secondary or continuation fund as compared to alternative options such as a fund extension or a traditional exit. | 6.11 Describe how the Firm discloses information regarding any related deals between the General Partner and acquirers (e.g., stapled transactions or side deals).
notes: ILPA 2.0 text lines 967-1053. The topic is new in 2.0: ILPA v1.2 has no matches for 'continuation' or 'GP-led'. Supporting template: Appendix G (GP-Led Secondaries / Continuation Funds).

question: What questions are asked under section 10.0 'ESG (Environmental, Social, Governance)' of the NJEDA Life Science Seed Fund due diligence questionnaire (Appendix A)?
gold_answer: Eight questions: 10.1 the role of the respondent's internal advisory board(s), all matters referred to them (including unresolved ones) and any other governing/advisory bodies; 10.2 conflicts of interest (potential, current, historic) and how they are identified, managed, disclosed (e.g. to the LPAC) and resolved, including any conflict committees; 10.3 the policy on personal investments by employees or affiliates in deals the respondent reviewed; 10.4 whether the respondent is a registered investment advisor (RIA); 10.5 the respondent's ESG-related policies and how ESG factors influence its investment beliefs; 10.6 the implementation status of its responsible investment policy and any plans to develop its approach to ESG; 10.7 how it contributes to portfolio companies' management of ESG risks and opportunities; 10.8 the monitoring processes it would use to assess the proposed Fund's portfolio companies' management of ESG factors.
gold_passage: 10.0 ESG (Environmental, Social, Governance) | 10.4. Is respondent a registered investment advisor (RIA)? | 10.5. What are respondent’s ESG-related policies and how do ESG factors influence respondent’s investment beliefs? | 10.8. What monitoring processes would respondent have in place to assess the proposed Fund’s portfolio companies’ management of ESG factors?
notes: NJEDA Appendix A, pages 20-21. Note that this ESG section also holds governance items (advisory boards, conflicts, personal investments, RIA status). A system that lists only 'ESG' topics is incomplete. Diversity and Inclusion is a separate section (2.0).

question: Which documents in the corpus mention the ISO 27001 information security standard, and in what context does each one use it?
gold_answer: Six documents. (1) ILPA DDQ 2.0, Q18.1.1: is the cyber/information security policy based on an internationally recognised standard (e.g. NIST or ISO 27001)? (2) INREV DDQ 2022 FoF/MM, Q3.3.2: is the manager compliant with ISO 27001 or other cyber/information security certifications? (3) INREV DDQ 2018 non-listed vehicles, Q3.3.1: the same compliance question. (4) SBCERS 2023 custody RFP: the provider must protect against unauthorised access, with assurance through ISO 27001 certification or reasonable analogues. (5) SC RSIC 2016 general consultant RFP: asks whether the service provider has other reports/certifications (ISO/IEC 27001, FISMA, FedRAMP, CJIS, etc.). (6) TRS Illinois FY25 private equity consultant RFP (contract terms): the contractor must run a written information security program in line with the ISO 27001 standard.
gold_passage: (e.g., NIST or ISO 27001)? | Are you compliant with International Organization for Standardization (ISO) 27001 or any other cyber security or information security certifications? | Are you compliant with ISO 27001 or any other cyber security or information security | through the receipt of ISO 27001 certification or reasonable analogues | RSIC data (i.e., ISO/IEC 27001, FISMA, FedRAMP, CJIS, etc.)? | improve a written information security program in accordance with the ISO 27001 standard
notes: Grep method: grep -il '27001' over all 81 text files gives exactly these 6. Variants also checked: 'ISO/IEC' and 'ISO.{0,30}27001' give the same 6. The 2022 INREV docx spells it '(ISO) 27001', so a search for the literal 'ISO 27001' misses it. The garbled INREV FoF .doc was decoded and has no '27001'. Passages are in the same order as the files. The topic spans DDQs and custody/consultant RFPs.

question: Which documents in the corpus directly ask whether the responding firm is a signatory to the (UN) Principles for Responsible Investment?
gold_answer: Four documents ask directly. (1) ILPA DDQ v1.2, Q10.2: 'Is the Firm a signatory to the United Nations Principles for Responsible Investing (UNPRI)?' (2) Illinois Firefighters' Pension Investment Fund private markets RFP (2023), Q28: the same wording. (3) SURS Illinois investment manager RFP template, Q85: is the firm a signatory to the PRI or a similar organization? (4) The older INREV DDQ for Fund of Funds and Multi-Managers (.doc), Q2.3.4: confirm whether you are a signatory to the UN PRI.
gold_passage: Is the Firm a signatory to the United Nations Principles for Responsible Investing (UNPRI)? | Is the firm a signatory to the United Nations Principles for Responsible Investing (UNPRI)? | Is your firm a signatory to the Principles for Responsible Investment (PRI) or a similar organization? | Please confirm whether you are a signatory to the UN Principles for Responsible Investment.
notes: Grep method: grep -in 'signator' plus 'UNPRI|UN PRI|PRI signator|Principles for Responsible Investment' over all 81 files, then each hit read by hand. Near misses, not counted: INPRS RFP 23-09 and MA PRIM RFP ask which initiatives the firm has adopted, giving UNPRI only as an example (partial credit is reasonable). INREV 2022 3.8.7 and the old .doc 2.3.3 ask how many underlying investments are PRI signatories. ILPA ESG Framework uses 'PRI signatory' as a bucket criterion. INREV 2018 lists UN PRI only as a social-policy standard. ILPA 2.0 asks about 'Diversity in Action signatory' only. The INREV .doc extraction is mostly garbled, but this line is readable.

question: Which RFPs in the corpus contain Iran-related certification, disclosure or compliance requirements for respondents?
gold_answer: Four RFPs. (1) Illinois SRS actuarial consulting RFP: the vendor must complete the 'Disclosure of Business Operations with Iran' form (Vendor Disclosure, Part 6). (2) LAFPP financial statement audit RFP: PSC-36 Iran Contracting Act; contractors on City contracts of $1,000,000 or more must submit the Iran Contracting Act of 2010 Compliance Affidavit. (3) NYC BERS RFP 2024-003 (investment consulting): the Iran Divestment Act Compliance Rider; each bidder must certify it is not on the State Finance Law §165-a list of entities engaged in investment activities in Iran. (4) SC RSIC 2016 general investment consultant RFP: Exhibit F, Iran Divestment Act of 2014 Certification, plus a consultant acknowledgement that RSIC may not invest in certain companies with business operations in Iran (and Sudan).
gold_passage: “Disclosure of Business Operations with Iran” form in Vendor Disclosure, Part 6. | are required to complete, sign, and submit the "Iran Contracting Act of 2010 Compliance Affidavit." | Each bidder or proposer must certify that it is not on the list of entities engaged in investment activities in Iran | Offeror must complete and submit with it Proposal Exhibit F – Iran Divestment Act of 2014
notes: Grep method: grep -il 'iran' over all 81 files gives exactly these 4, and every matched word is 'Iran'/'IRAN' (no false positives like 'Miranda'). The answer spans actuarial, audit and consultant RFPs. Near miss: INPRS RFP 22-04 (core plus fixed income) requires a 'Sudan and Terror States compliance screen' under Indiana law but does not name Iran, so it is excluded (partial credit is reasonable). COAERS RFPs require only that respondents are not on the terrorism watch list.

question: Apart from ILPA's own publications and the PRI covering note, which documents in the corpus refer to ILPA, and for what purpose?
gold_answer: Four documents. (1) Arizona PSPRS investment consultant RFP: consultant databases of managers' deal histories should include the portfolio metrics ILPA recommends for collection. (3) NYC BERS RFP 2024-003: the consultant must give ILPA transaction types per the ILPA Capital Call & Distribution Notice Template and keep cash-flow records on that basis. (4) NJEDA Life Science Seed Fund DDQ, Q7.3: asks whether the respondent's standard reporting package will be modelled on ILPA Reporting Best Practices.

notes: Grep method: grep -ic 'ILPA' over all 81 files. Non-zero counts are the 5 ILPA files, the PRI note (excluded by the question), Arizona PSPRS (1), Missouri LAGERS (1), NYC BERS (5) and NJEDA (1). grep -il 'Institutional Limited Partners' matches only ILPA files. The INREV files, including the decoded .doc, do not mention ILPA.

gold_answer: NOT IN CORPUS

question: What annual fee does the Texas Municipal Retirement System (TMRS) currently pay its incumbent general investment consultant?
gold_answer: NOT IN CORPUS
notes: The TMRS general investment consulting RFP mentions 'TMRS’ incumbent consultant' once (onboarding question, line 690) but gives no name and no current fee. Its fee content is the respondent's own Section VIII Fee Proposal. The TMRS global custody RFP lists RVK, Inc. as the designated contact for that custody search, but it does not say RVK is the general investment consultant and gives no fee. grep 'incumbent|current consultant|retainer|annual fee' across both TMRS files finds no amount. The 'annual fee' hits are the respondent's fee-proposal instruction (line 956) and the sample contract clause 3.1, where the fee is blank ('($________)'), plus the custody RFP's fee schedules for respondents. Tempting because the $36 billion system size and fee sections are nearby.
